extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulatory commenters, legal/regulatory researchers, and regulated entities (e.g., mine operators, independent contractors) searching Federal Register documents about independent-contractor-related rules
extracted.subtask_description: A JSON search-results listing of Federal Register entries matching the term 'independent contractor', aggregating proposed rules, notices, and final rules across multiple agencies. The page collects excerpts and metadata from many regulatory documents that mention independent contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: specialized_skills_business_initiative_test
rubrics_metrics.description: “Where the worker brings specialized skills to the work relationship, this fact is not itself indicative of independent contractor status because both employees and independent contractors may be skilled workers. It is the worker's use of those specialized skills in connection with business-like initiative that indicates that the worker is an independent contractor.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance stresses that specialized skills alone do not establish independent-contractor status; evaluators must look for use of skills together with business-like initiative (e.g., marketing, setting prices, bearing business risk). This language appears as an additional consideration for the factor assessing specialized skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: economic_reality_independent_contractor_definition
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this rule, the term “independent contractor” refers to workers who, as a matter of economic reality, are not economically dependent on an employer for work and are in business for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the definitional standard for classification under the referenced DOL rule — an economic-dependence (economic reality) test rather than labels. Notes that such workers are commonly called independent contractor, self-employed, or freelancer, and the rule is not intended to disrupt bona fide independent contractors' businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: msha_independent_contractor_registration_and_identification
rubrics_metrics.description: 30 CFR part 45 information requirements and procedures for independent contractors to obtain a Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) identification number (IN); independent contractors applying for IN numbers must submit MSHA Form 7000-52; MSHA assigns an IN if requested or issues an IN the first time the independent contractor is cited for a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page excerpts reference that MSHA collects hours worked by the independent contractor on mine property for the previous calendar year and maintains a register disclosure of all independent contractors working at a mine. The information collection supports appropriate assessment of fines for violations by independent contractors and the deterrent effect of enforcement. Practical implication: independent contractors working at mines must register and provide specified data (Form 7000-52 and hours/worksite info).

rubrics_metrics.name: paperwork_reduction_act_information_collection_standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA), agencies must solicit public comment on proposed collections to ensure that requested data can be provided in the desired format, reporting burden (time and financial resources) is minimized, collection instruments are clearly understood, and the impact of collection requirements on respondents can be properly assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the procedural/quality standard applied when agencies (e.g., DOL/MSHA) publish information-collection notices. When preparing or commenting on PRA notices, assess clarity, format, burden, and respondent impact; provide evidence or estimates to support claims about burden or format feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: petition_for_modification_procedure_for_mine_safety_standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's regulations at 30 CFR 44.9, 44.10, and 44.11 provide procedures by which a mine operator, representative of miners, or independent contractor may request relief from a mandatory safety standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates who may file petitions for modification and points readers to the cited CFR provisions for procedural requirements. For commenters: petitions must follow the specified regulatory process (see 30 CFR 44.9-44.11) and supporting information should demonstrate need for relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: regulatory_definition_inclusion_of_independent_contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple agency rule excerpts (e.g., FRA regulations) explicitly define regulatory scope to include independent contractors: '...any independent contractor providing goods or services to a railroad; and any employee of such ... independent contractor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies enumerate covered persons/entities, independent contractors are explicitly included; this affects who is subject to regulatory duties, enforcement, and penalties. Drafting or commenting on rules should account for how inclusion/definition affects obligations of contractors and their employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: civil_penalty_and_enforcement_application_to_independent_contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text states that persons (including independent contractors) who violate requirements are subject to civil penalties (at least the minimum civil monetary penalty and up to the ordinary maximum), and that each day a violation continues constitutes a separate offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical enforcement standard: independent contractors can be assessed civil penalties like other regulated entities; commenters should note potential per-day aggregation of penalties and check agency-specific penalty policies (agency website referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: use_of_independent_contractors_for_assessments_and_public_comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices state that agencies (e.g., FDA) sometimes commission independent contractors to perform assessments (e.g., hiring and retention assessments, communications assessments) and publish final reports to solicit public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies rely on contractor assessments to fulfill statutory or program commitments (e.g., PDUFA), the published reports are subject to public comment; commenters can address methodology, findings, and recommendations in those contractor reports.
